correctness.rationale: For every crown graph, total domination is equivalent to at least two selected vertices on each side. Profile-sum admissibility follows exactly. The deficit argument proves uniqueness of two opposite mixed triples for \(n\ge5\), and bounds the \(\(n=3\),4\) extrema. The factorial profile weight counts unlabelled-block partitions of labelled vertices; all small exceptional profile types have been exhausted, and separate adjacency-level set-partition enumeration agrees at \(\(\(n=3\),4\),5\). No infinite conclusion is inferred from finite experiments.

value.rationale: A natural regular bipartite graph obtained by deleting one perfect matching exhibits a structural decrease of the maximum coalition partition count from the full vertex set size to 2n-4. The sharp deficit, uniqueness of the optimal block profile, and exact all-n optimum census describe nontrivial partition structure, not simply a small scalar improvement; the \(n=4\) exception has an explicit exact finite count.
